title: The Master Builder
wpTitle: West End Reviews for My Master Builder starring Ewan McGregor, Elizabeth Debicki & Kate Fleetwood

ratings.excerpt: Ewan McGregor makes an exquisite return to UK theatre in My Master Builder … American playwright Lila Raicek offers a punchy and poisonous spin on Ibsen’s original play … In the lead role Ewan McGregor buzzes with charisma as he returns to the London stage after many years’ absence. … Elena, beautifully played with brittle bitterness by Fleetwood, has all the world weariness of a successful woman for ever overlooked in favour of her even more famous spouse. … Michael Grandage’s robustly elegant production guides us confidently through Raicek’s appealingly murky mixture of sex, power and professional status, using Elena to demonstrate how female empowerment and solidarity can curdle when it comes to sexual jealousy.

Ewan McGregor’s cheating starchitect is torn down … Ibsen is moved to the Hamptons in Lila Raicek’s play, co-starring Kate Fleetwood and Elizabeth Debicki, about the destruction wreaked by adultery … Henrik Ibsen’s Icarus-like architect is indubitably the patrician protagonist of his play The Master Builder... In Lila Raicek’s modern take, his wife – clever, accomplished and angry – is the fulcrum. … Fleetwood is magnetic as Elena and she eclipses McGregor, who is boyishly earnest in his relationship with Mathilde, despite playing the older man. He seems genuinely in love and does not have the bearing of the narcissist he is supposed to be. Ewan McGregor struggles to raise the roof in his stage return … Back on the London stage after 17 years, McGregor’s allure is undimmed but he fails to summon the necessary intensity for Ibsen’s tragedy … Thanks not least to Star Wars, McGregor’s name remains no small box-office draw. Yet, while it’s nice to have him treading the boards again – his allure undimmed – he struggles to attain the intensity required to raise the roof as Solness, a Scot-Brit “starchitect … Given how often of late high-profile men have reaped the whirlwind of rapacious behaviour, the work seems ripe for a topical update. Ewan McGregor’s cheating architect is undone at a Hamptons party from hell in My Master Builder … In this feminist reimagining of Ibsen’s original, the actor’s star power is outshone by his formidable co-star Kate Fleetwood … Lila Raicek’s feminist reimagining of Ibsen’s The Master Builder should be obligatory viewing for the put-upon wives of TV’s Grand Designs … Here, Ewan McGregor brings serious charm to the role of the titular architect Henry Solness, but his star power is entirely outshone by Kate Fleetwood’s formidable acting chops as his furious wife Elena, bent on bringing his dreams crashing down to the ground. … ... This Ewan McGregor-starring Ibsen rewrite is thoughtful but lacking in fireworks … Having now seen My Master Builder I’m not sure I’m any the wiser as to what the big secret was. Perhaps it’s simply that a full plot summary felt like it was virtually begging interviewers to ask star Ewan McGregor about the end of his first marriage. … The original Master Builder is a weird, stodgy play, and Raicek’s version does a lot to address its issues: there are much better female characters and none of the old stultifying symbolism. … The main trouble is that there is a power imbalance within Michael Grandage’s production: Debicki and Fleetwood are hardly nobodies, but McGregor is the big name in this female-centric rewriting of Ibsen. … ... taking pains to make Henry broadly inoffensive leaves him a

Ewan McGregor struggles to animate My Master Builder … Lila Raicek’s play is a wooden and contrived take on Ibsen’s drama at Wyndham’s Theatre, London … ... timely as all this is, the situation feels oddly contrived and the dialogue often stiff and airless. … ... the usually excellent Michael Grandage directs with pace. But not even he can solve the melodramatic ending. This new piece feels like one of those renovations that hasn’t quite worked.

Ewan McGregor can’t save a dodgy Ibsen revamp … Kudos to the A-lister for appearing on a London stage for the first time in nearly 20 years, yet he doesn’t have the gravitas needed … This is going to be a test of faith for Ewan McGregor’s admirers. How much are they willing to endure to see him in the flesh in a painfully windy psychodrama, modelled on Ibsen’s The Master Builder, which grinds its way to a wildly implausible conclusion? … ... the truth is that he simply doesn’t have the gravitas needed for the role of a superstar architect whose personal life is about to implode. … In so far as she beefs up the roles of the spouse and the younger woman who watch the hero self-destruct, she has improved on the overwrought original. Ewan McGregor's first stage appearance in 17 years is a dud … This play boasts a glib, howlingly pretentious script and a drippy central character in McGregor’s architect Henry Solness … Gratifying as it is to see Ewan McGregor back on stage after 17 years, I wish he’d found a better vehicle than this so-called “new play … Michael Grandage’s brisk take on the glib, howlingly pretentious script can be enjoyed as a guilty pleasure, a celeb-heavy melodrama of sex and power that owes more to Fifty Shades of Grey than to serious #MeToo fictions. But really, it’s a load of old nonsense. … The truly weird thing about this pairing of star and material is that McGregor’s character, international architect Henry Solness is a drippy blank. … Kate Fleetwood plays Solness’s wife Elena in full-on, steel

Ibsen spin-off with Ewan McGregor is ill-constructed … The intention is clearly to turn Ibsen’s musings on male creativity and potency into a more relevant discussion of sexual politics. … The language constantly strives for the poetic but becomes impossibly stilted, leaving the actors making speeches at each other rather than interacting. McGregor in particular, making his return to the London stage after 17 years, seems desperately uncomfortable. … Only Fleetwood thrives, endowing Elena with a fierce energy, her eyes narrowing as she contrives her moment of reckoning. But in trying to reshape the play and give the women some agency, Raicek simply creates new problems.

Insubstantial riff on Ibsen … Ewan McGregor and Elizabeth Debicki star in a glossy, contrived response to Ibsen’s classic … Successful older man betrays his wife to exploit the infatuation of a young, beautiful woman: it’s an everyday tale of sexual politics and banal midlife crisis. John Lithgow v Ewan McGregor — there’s only one winner … The Trainspotting actor returns to the British stage at last … ... My Master Builder, a new play by the American Lila Raicek inspired by Ibsen’s The Master Builder, has aspirations to profundity that are washed away by its hokeyness. Ewan McGregor, in his first British stage role since 2007, is thoroughly unconvincing as the title character … Kate Fleetwood is exceptional as Solness’s wife, Elena, an outspoken publishing bigwig readying to divorce him. … Yet fitful moments of raw insight about marriage are obliterated by line after line of characters reminding each other of shared experiences, of soapish grandiosity … The director Michael Grandage, normally excellent, can do nothing to curb the risible stiltedness of it all
